Sydney Industrial Coatings — Shopify Migration & Redesign Proposal

Client: Sydney Industrial Coatings (sydneyindustrialcoatings.com.au) — Sydney-based distributor of epoxy flooring products and floor grinders (hire & sales), part of Epoxy Warehouse

After Epoxy Warehouse, you asked us to look at Sydney Industrial Coatings again and come back with recommendations — particularly for the homepage and menu — ahead of migrating to Shopify. This proposal covers what we found reviewing the current site, our UX recommendations, the three feature questions from our last round of notes (rental, calculator, shipping calculator), and the full effort and cost to build it.

1

Where you are today

The current site runs on WooCommerce, with a flat top-level menu — Home, Shop, Training Courses, About Us, Contact Us, Reviews — plus a Hire Shop category tucked into the footer. It doesn't make clear upfront that you run two different businesses under one roof: buying epoxy products, and hiring floor prep equipment.

The homepage leans on long blocks of descriptive text — "Why Us", "Manufacturers & Brands", "Our Products & Systems" and similar sections — repeated in paragraph form rather than broken into points a visitor can scan. The catalogue itself is substantial: eight coating-system categories (Solid Colour, Flake, Metallic, Clear Finish/Concrete Sealers, Cementitious Polyurethane, Self Levelling & Repair, Traffic & Safety, Accessories) and close to 30 brands, none of which surface in the main navigation today.

Why this matters: the site currently reads like classic SEO-era copywriting — long text meant for search engines rather than a shopper deciding what to buy. That's not a fit for how people actually shop online now, and it's the main thing a redesign needs to fix, alongside the navigation.
2

UX & design recommendations

Built on Ella (§5). UX is the priority here — UI naturally comes with it, but the goal is a site that guides two different customer journeys (buy vs. hire) rather than one that just looks refreshed.

AreaWhat we see todayWhat we'd do
MenuOne flat list; Shop and Services aren't visually separated, and brands don't appear in navigation at allSplit the menu into two clear paths: Shop (mega menu, grouped into parent/child categories — e.g. Floor Coatings with Accessories, Repair & Mortars as sub-items, using your own product knowledge to group them correctly) plus a dedicated Brands entry, since shoppers who already know their brand should be able to jump straight there; and Services (Training Courses, Equipment Hire)
SearchStandard WooCommerce search boxAdd predictive/smart search suggestions as people type
HomepageLong descriptive paragraphs repeated across several sections; brand names listed as plain text linksBreak the text into short, scannable points; add dedicated sections for your two core services (product sales + equipment hire) instead of paragraphs about them; turn the brand list into a visual brand section
Live chatNoneAdd live chat so visitors can get help picking the right system or product; if no one's online, fall back to a WhatsApp link so the question still reaches you
Collection pagesCategory grid with no visible filteringAdd filters for price, stock and brand — sidebar or top bar
Product pageColour/variant picked via a dropdown select, with size shown only after selectingShow the matching size as a plain list instead of a dropdown, so every option is visible at a glance
MobileNot optimised; no sticky navigationDesign mobile-first — decisive for conversion in the building-materials and industrial-equipment space — with a sticky mobile menu

3

Feature clarifications — following up on your latest points

3.1 Equipment rental (Hire Shop)

We're not yet fully clear on your detailed rental flow and rules, so we did some research based on our current understanding and found BookThatApp as a possible fit. Could you review it from your side and confirm whether it generally matches what you have in mind? Once confirmed, we'll size the setup hours — they're not yet in the estimate below.

3.2 Calculator

Your current calculator is built on the ACF plugin plus custom code; we haven't found a Shopify app that replicates it directly. We'll rebuild it as Shopify metafields, with the formula and display logic added into the theme.

On data: we checked with your migration team, and they've confirmed the existing WooCommerce calculator data can be imported into the new metafields — they've already shared their own cost for that migration work, which is separate from this quote.

Effort: 15 working hours, part of the 60h build line in §6. The reason it's not a quick job: your product structure isn't fully consistent — some products use around 5 calculator fields (a show/hide toggle, litres-per-sqm consumption rate, plus three others), while others have 2–3 rows in the product-quantity section, up to 13 fields, which needs more flexible logic. You can decide which site — Sydney Industrial Coatings or Epoxy Warehouse — gets this built first.

Screenshot from your WooCommerce admin (ACF fields referenced in your note): the Show Calculator toggle, L consumption rate/sqm, and the Product coverage / Description text / Price per can row — one of the simpler products, with only the base 5 fields.

7

Who configures what

Payment and shipping are configured by you, in your own Shopify admin. We advise, document and verify — we don't enter the credentials.

This is deliberate. Connecting a payment provider means handling merchant credentials and API keys that are financial access to your business, and a shipping account carries your commercial rate agreement. Those belong with the account holder, not an agency — and it means no third party ever holds a live key to your money. Everything else in this proposal is built by us as normal.

ItemYou doWe do
Payment providerOpen the merchant account, enter the credentials in Shopify admin, run the first live transactionRecommend the provider, supply a step-by-step setup guide, and verify checkout end to end afterwards
Shipping zones & ratesEnter the zones and rate tiers in Shopify admin — Australia-wide, as today — and keep them updated when your carrier revises pricesTurn your current shipping terms into an exact zone-and-rate sheet, walk you through entering it, then test real destinations and weights at checkout

This does not reduce the quote: the configuration time is replaced by time writing the guide and verifying the result afterwards.

Happy to walk through any of this on a call if that's easier than reading it.
